title: Injective module sheaves are acyclic after forgetting to abelian sheaves
statement: Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site, i.e. a site $\mathcal C$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with a sheaf of rings $\mathcal O$, let $U$ be an object of $\mathcal C$, and let $I$ be an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions] of the abelian category of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ for the underlying sheaf of abelian groups. Then $H^q(U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every $q>0$, where $H^q(U,-)$ is the cohomology over $U$ computed in the category $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)$ of abelian sheaves, the right derived functors of $\Gamma(U,-)$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology].

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree), proof, second paragraph, via Lemmas 03FC and 03F9

proof.text: For every covering $\mathcal U$ of every object $U$, the injective module Cech lemma [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-injective-module-cech-acyclic] gives $\check H^p(\mathcal U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for all $p>0$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 03FD, proof, second paragraph via Lemma Tag 03FC

proof.text: Apply the Cech-to-derived vanishing criterion [lem-weil-pbc-site-cech-vanishing-criterion] to the abelian sheaf $I_{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $\mathcal B=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $\mathrm{Cov}$ the set of all coverings of $\mathcal C$. Its assumptions (1) and (2) hold trivially (every object lies in $\mathcal B$, and every covering of an object is refined by itself, which lies in $\mathrm{Cov}$), and its assumption (3) is the vanishing established in Step 1. It yields $H^q(U,I_{\mathrm{ab}})=0$ for every object $U$ and every $q>0$.
